title: Cartesian and Boolean products of groups
notes: Only the heading \ru{Декартово и булево произведение групп} survives before the change to resolution.
statement: No groups, category, construction of a Boolean product, or assertion are specified. The phrase cannot determine one mathematical item more precisely.
fate: Title searches distinguish several uses of Boolean products; none can identify the intended construction from this heading. No publication match is asserted.
present_status: As of November 2026: Unidentified heading, rather than evidence of an undeveloped problem.

title: Hironaka resolution in characteristic zero
notes: A singular divisor \(D\) is replaced by a smooth hypersurface over it, under the heading Hironaka. The base field and the distinction between total and strict transforms are not stated.
statement: For a reduced variety over a characteristic-zero field, resolution gives a proper birational morphism from a smooth variety, an isomorphism over a prescribed smooth locus. In embedded resolution of a divisor in a smooth ambient variety, the strict transform is smooth and the total transform has simple normal crossings after suitable blowups; the total inverse image need not be a smooth hypersurface.
reconstruction: The field hypothesis and strict/total-transform distinction are editorial precisions.
fate: The named result had appeared in \citet{hironaka1964resolution}, Part I, introduction and main theorem, in 1964, before this September discussion; the Russian translation followed in 1965. The opened archive record verifies the publication, not every proof in the 95-page paper.
present_status: As of November 2026: The characteristic-zero theorem is established. Removing the characteristic-zero hypothesis is a different question and is not posed here.

title: Universal blowup and invertibility of the center
notes: The notebook seeks \(V'\to V\) making an ideal \(J\) locally principal, with a universal mapping property, and then writes its symmetric tensor algebra.
statement: For a scheme \(X\) and a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal \(I\), the blowup is \(\operatorname{Proj}_X\mathcal R(I)\), where \(\mathcal R(I)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}I^n\). It is terminal among \(X\)-schemes on which the inverse-image ideal defines an effective Cartier divisor. Locally principal alone is insufficient when a generator is a zero divisor. In general \(\operatorname{Sym}(I)\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal R(I)\) is not an isomorphism.
reconstruction: Replace the symmetric algebra by the Rees algebra in the general assertion; retain the original notation in the notes field.
fate: This is the standard blowup universal property, recorded precisely in \citet[tags 01OF and 0806]{stacks2026blowups}. The modern reference is used to correct the algebra, not to date its invention. The pre-seminar source is \citet[Chapter II, Section 8.1]{grothendieck1961ega2} (1961); its publisher metadata were opened, but the 27 MB scan exceeded the retrieval limit. The exact modern construction was checked in Stacks.
present_status: As of November 2026: Established construction. The symmetric algebra works for ideals of linear type, including the two regular-sequence examples below.

title: Proj, homogeneous primes, and the local sheaf
notes: Homogeneous prime ideals and homogeneous fractions of equal degree are discussed; the abbreviation \ru{Выбр.} precedes primes containing all positive-degree elements.
statement: For a positively graded ring \(S\), \(\operatorname{Proj}S\) consists of homogeneous primes not containing \(S_+=\bigoplus_{d>0}S_d\). On \(D_+(f)\), \(\mathcal O\) is the degree-zero part of \(S_f\); the degree-one component gives \(\mathcal O(1)\), with the usual degree conventions.
reconstruction: The intended exclusion and the distinction between degree zero and degree one are explicit modern reconstructions.
fate: The projective-spectrum construction underlying \citet[Section 31.33]{stacks2026blowups} predates the lecture. The scan supports the abbreviation but does not justify expanding it as ``choose'' rather than ``discard. The pre-seminar source is \citet[Chapter II, Section 8.1]{grothendieck1961ega2} (1961); its publisher metadata were opened, but the 27 MB scan exceeded the retrieval limit. The exact modern construction was checked in Stacks.
present_status: As of November 2026: Standard scheme construction; reversing the irrelevant-ideal exclusion would destroy the intended Proj.

title: Blowing up the origin of the affine plane
notes: For the ideal of the origin in the plane the exceptional fiber is a projective line and local coordinate ratios are introduced.
statement: For \(I=(x,y)\subset k[x,y]\), \(\operatorname{Bl}_0\mathbb A^2\subset\mathbb A^2\times\mathbb P^1\) has equation \(xV=yU\). Its two charts are \(y=xv\) and \(x=yu\), each an affine plane, and the fiber over the origin is \(\mathbb P^1_k\).
reconstruction: The homogeneous-coordinate equation and chart equations spell out the drawing.
fate: This is the affine-chart construction of \citet[Lemma 31.33.2]{stacks2026blowups}; the notebook example is an exposition of it. The pre-seminar source is \citet[Chapter II, Section 8.1]{grothendieck1961ega2} (1961); its publisher metadata were opened, but the 27 MB scan exceeded the retrieval limit. The exact modern construction was checked in Stacks.
present_status: As of November 2026: The calculation is valid over any field and gives a smooth blowup.

title: Blowing up the crossing ideal (z,xy)
notes: The next center is \(z=0,xy=0\), the union of two lines, with the two generators \(z,xy\).
statement: For \(I=(z,xy)\subset k[x,y,z]\), the Rees presentation is \(k[x,y,z,U,V]/(xyU-zV)\). On \(U\ne0\) the chart is \(xy=zv\); on \(V\ne0\) it is \(z=xyu\). The former has a singular point at the origin; therefore this single blowup is not a general resolution procedure.
reconstruction: The Rees relation, two charts, and singular-point diagnosis are editorial algebraic checks; the notebook does not claim a completed resolution.
fate: The example is an application of the blowup charts in \citet[Lemma 31.33.2]{stacks2026blowups}. No later publication is needed to account for it. The pre-seminar source is \citet[Chapter II, Section 8.1]{grothendieck1961ega2} (1961); its publisher metadata were opened, but the 27 MB scan exceeded the retrieval limit. The exact modern construction was checked in Stacks.
present_status: As of November 2026: The calculation remains a useful warning that an arbitrary center can produce a singular blowup.

title: Canonical lattice gas and Ising energy
notes: There are \(N\) particles at distinct sites of a lattice box of volume \(V\), with energy minus the number of occupied nearest-neighbor pairs and weights \(e^{-U/T}\).
statement: Let \(\Lambda\subset\mathbb Z^\nu\) be finite, \(\eta_x\in\{0,1\}\), \(\sum_x\eta_x=N\), and \(H_\Lambda(\eta)=-\sum_{\{x,y\}\subset\Lambda,\,|x-y|_1=1}\eta_x\eta_y\). At \(T>0\), \(Z_{\Lambda,N}=\sum e^{-H_\Lambda/T}\) and the canonical law is the normalized weight. With \(\eta_x=(1+\sigma_x)/2\) this is an Ising model with the corresponding fixed magnetization and boundary terms.
fate: The model is the starting point of \citet[Section 1]{dobrushin1965phase}; its definition predates the lecture. That paper was received on 30 September 1964 and published in 1965.
present_status: As of November 2026: Standard finite-volume probability law; the sum counts configurations once, not ordered particle labels.

title: Thermodynamic limit and independence of regular shape
notes: The notes introduce \(f(v,T)=\lim N^{-1}\log Z\), \(v=V/N\), assert independence of the expanding region, and call the resulting function convex.
statement: For this finite-range lattice gas along regular expanding boxes, with \(N/|\Lambda|\to\rho\in(0,1)\), the canonical log-partition density \(s_T(\rho)=\lim|\Lambda|^{-1}\log Z_{\Lambda,N}\) exists and is concave. Its perspective \(f(v,T)=v s_T(1/v)\), \(v>1\), is concave. Boundary changes of order \(|\partial\Lambda|\) do not affect the limit for van Hove sequences.
reconstruction: A single positive-log convention is imposed; regularity of the exhausting sequence is supplied.
fate: \citet[Section 1]{dobrushin1965phase} explicitly uses the thermodynamic limit as prior input. The positive-log convention in the notebook forces concavity; its later minus sign cannot be retained simultaneously.
present_status: As of November 2026: Established for the stated finite-range interaction and regular limits. Arbitrary irregular regions need not have negligible boundary effects.

title: Coexistence plateau and the meaning of one transition
notes: A pressure plateau is drawn and the van der Waals picture is compared with the lattice model; one line later says \(\partial f/\partial v=0\).
statement: For \(F=-NT f(v,T)\), pressure is \(p=T\partial_v f\) wherever the derivative exists. A coexistence interval is an affine segment of \(f\), hence a constant-pressure interval; the pressure need not be zero. In density variables, the grand-canonical transition corresponds to distinct equilibrium densities at one chemical potential.
reconstruction: The relationship between canonical and grand-canonical variables is made explicit; ``zero derivative is replaced by ``constant derivative.
fate: The thermodynamic interpretation is the framework of \citet[Section 1 and Theorem 1]{dobrushin1965phase}. The general claim of exactly one transition is not justified by the sketch alone.
present_status: As of November 2026: Phase coexistence is rigorous at sufficiently low temperature in the models discussed; the picture is not a proof of a complete phase diagram.

title: No positive-temperature transition in one dimension
notes: The one-dimensional model is said to have no phase transition at positive temperature.
statement: The nearest-neighbor one-dimensional Ising model has analytic infinite-volume pressure for every finite real field and \(T>0\), because its positive transfer matrix has a simple Perron eigenvalue. Its canonical free energy has no low-temperature coexistence segment of the type sought in dimensions two and three.
fate: This classical contrast is part of the introduction in \citet{dobrushin1965phase}; the transfer-matrix mechanism predates 1964.
present_status: As of November 2026: Established for finite-range one-dimensional Ising interactions; long-range interactions are outside the statement.

title: Onsager and Kac--Helfand antecedents
notes: Onsager's two-dimensional result and work attributed to Kac and Helfand are named as earlier achievements, without a complete bibliographic or parameter specification.
statement: Onsager solved the zero-field nearest-neighbor square-lattice Ising free energy. The Kac--Helfand reference is an antecedent in the discussion of phase transition, but the notebook alone does not identify a particular long-range limiting regime.
fate: The prior literature is discussed in \citet[Section 1 and bibliography]{dobrushin1965phase}. The Onsager identification is secure; a unique Kac--Helfand theorem is not inferred merely from the names.
present_status: As of November 2026: The historical comparison is expository. It must not be read as an exact solution of the three-dimensional model.

title: Macroscopic density deviations and coexistence
notes: The number of particles in a macroscopic subcube is compared with its expected density. Failure of a volume-scale exponential deviation bound is used to detect a linear piece of the limiting free energy.
statement: For a fixed volume fraction \(a\in(0,1)\), compare a density split \(\rho=a\rho_1+(1-a)\rho_2\). Up to subvolume boundary errors the log probability has volume rate \(a s_T(\rho_1)+(1-a)s_T(\rho_2)-s_T(\rho)\). Strict inequality gives exponential suppression; equality along an interval is the canonical signature of coexistence. The criterion requires the allowed density splits and thermodynamic sequences to be specified.
reconstruction: The rate function and the precise role of concavity replace compressed probability notation.
fate: The matching criterion appears in \citet[Theorem 2 and the reduction following it]{dobrushin1965phase}, received nine days after the seminar and published in 1965. The shorter \citet{dobrushin1965announcement} was received and presented by Kolmogorov on 15 September 1964, then published in 1965. Receipt and presentation are recorded separately from publication; no earlier public distribution date is inferred.
present_status: As of November 2026: The criterion is established in this lattice-gas setting. A failure of an unspecified law of large numbers in an arbitrary model is not an equivalent theorem.

reconstruction: The dependence on dimension and temperature is restored.

title: Contour entropy against Boltzmann cost
notes: The proof counts contours by exponential bounds, including \(3^k\), and compares their multiplicity with the energetic penalty.
statement: A rooted planar nearest-neighbor contour with a prescribed first edge has at most \(3^{k-1}\) nonbacktracking continuations of length \(k\); self-avoidance only decreases that number. In higher dimensions a separate connected-surface enumeration supplies \(C^k\). If the energy cost per unit interface exceeds \(T\log C\), the contour sum converges.
fate: This is the entropy-energy estimate in \citet[Sections 3--4]{dobrushin1965phase}. The seminar's planar \(3^k\) cannot by itself enumerate arbitrary three-dimensional surfaces. The shorter \citet{dobrushin1965announcement} was received and presented by Kolmogorov on 15 September 1964, then published in 1965. Receipt and presentation are recorded separately from publication; no earlier public distribution date is inferred. \citet[paragraphs 1--2]{dobrushin1966addendum} repairs an error in Lemma 4 by grouping adjacent contours into generalized cycles and also corrects inequality (8.8); the original coexistence conclusion and its \(Q(T)\) are preserved.
present_status: As of November 2026: Rigorous with a specified root and contour class; it is the low-temperature Peierls mechanism.
